Networking is the practice of meeting other people involved in the same kind of work, to share information, support each other etc.  Before you start networking, you should assess your interests and skills and a field you want to investigate. Then, you identify potential professionals to contact. Here are some tips to help you:
<li>Identify the people you would like to speak with. Often, they are people you have had some contact with, like a former colleague or teacher.
<li>Treat the interview as a serious occasion. Dress appropriately and arrive 15 minutes early.
<li>Very busy people may prefer to have a phone interview. Be flexible in scheduling.
<li>If you do not hear back from the person, wait at least one week before contacting them again.
<li>Remember to follow up with a thank you message.

images.text: In the business world, not all interviews are job interviews. While the word “interview” usually represents a formal meeting organized to help an employer assess the quality of candidates for a particular job, it could equally be arranged for different purposes. An example is the informational interview.

An informational interview is usually initiated by a person who would like to connect with someone who has firsthand experience working in a certain area. They may want to know about future prospects or challenges in the field. The immediate goal is not to obtain a job, but rather to network with people who are working in a given field. A person who initiates an informational interview probably has an interest in working in the field, or may see the potential for collaborating at some point in the future. In either case, an honest discussion about information related to the business can be very useful.

It is common to invite someone you know already to an informational interview, like a former teacher or colleague. It is important to treat the informational interview as a formal meeting. You should follow the same social norms as any interview, including wearing formal attire and arriving 15 minutes early. After preparing specific questions, you should let the conversation flow in a direction that appears useful and interesting to both participants. Prepared questions should not dictate the whole meeting. By wrapping up the meeting after about 30 minutes, you show your respect for your contact.

At the end of the interview, it is acceptable to ask for the contact information of other people who would be willing to meet you. Networking is a continual process of growth that is important for everyone in business. Always thank the person by sending a letter or e-mail as a follow-up.
